decisions.executionNote: Start a continuous elbow-up right-hand approach to the key; keep the left arm parked.
Continue the right wrist overhead arc toward the visible key, with small continuous orientation increments.
Move toward the key's more forward live position while bringing the gripper into a downward grasp orientation.
Align the open right gripper with the live key's slanted shaft and finish the overhead approach.
Use wrist RGB to center the key's lower shaft between the open fingers, correcting the small downward-axis tilt.
Fine lateral centering from the right wrist view before closing; match the shaft angle and maintain table clearance.
Correct the final small shaft angle and close the right fingers around the key's lower shaft.
Let the right grip finish closing, then begin a small lift to check key retention visually.
The key is visible between the closed fingers. Lift it clear while beginning a slow yaw adjustment toward the central handover.
Carry the retained key toward the center at safe height, rotating gradually for a side-on left-hand regrasp.
Raise and yaw the key for handover while starting the left elbow-up approach in its own workspace.
Bring the right-hand key to central transfer height; continue the left wrist's upward and inward arc without crossing arms.
Complete most of the right key yaw adjustment and advance the left open hand along a continuous elbow-up arc toward the transfer.
Approach the left-side pre-transfer pose while holding the right-hand key steady and finishing its yaw alignment.
Finish orienting the left gripper side-on to the exposed key bow, stopping short for visual alignment before transfer.
Replan with smaller wrist increments after the continuity guard, reaching a side-on pre-transfer pose with a partly open left grip.
Advance the left gripper along the exposed bow while the right hand holds the key fixed; retain a partial opening for alignment.
Lower and advance the left fingers slightly to center the bow in the wrist view before taking the key.
The bow shifted during the approach. Open and back the left hand off slightly while retaining the right grip, to avoid forcing the transfer.
Recenter the shifted key bow using the left wrist view with fully open fingers, approaching slowly without releasing the donor.
Center the left fingers around the bow's new position, then begin closing while the right hand remains fixed.
Finish centering the bow and close the left gripper fully; keep both wrists stationary while the fingers settle.
The left fingers surround the bow. Release the right donor gradually while keeping the left grip closed and both wrists still.
The key fell during release. Retract the left hand and bring the open right gripper back over the visible key for a controlled recovery.
Descend toward the recovered key's lower shaft, adjusting yaw from the wrist image with the left arm held clear.
Continue the recovery descent and align the open fingers with the key's observed shaft direction.
Fine-center the recovered key's lower shaft, then close the right gripper at tabletop grasp height.
Allow the recovered-key grip to close fully, then make a small retention-check lift before retrying the handover.
Lift the recovered key clear and restore a controlled near-central yaw for a more accurately aligned transfer.
Raise the retained key toward transfer height, keeping its shaft steady and the receiving hand clear.
Bring the stable key up to the receiving hand's height before any further contact.
Before advancing, align the receiving hand vertically and laterally with the key bow using the left wrist view; donor stays closed.
Advance the fully open receiving fingers toward the bow along the hand axis, correcting only the small height offset.
The bow is now centered at the left fingers in wrist RGB. Close the receiving grip without moving either wrist.
Let the receiving fingers finish closing, then cautiously relax the donor while checking that the bow stays between the left pads.
The bow is slipping outside the receiving pads. Re-secure the donor and reopen/lower the left hand slightly before another closure.
The key has dropped again. Separate the hands and lower the open donor toward the table to reacquire it safely.
Reorient the recovery grasp to the key's changed tabletop direction while descending with both hands separated.
Align the recovery grasp parallel to the key's shaft and approach just above tabletop height.
Move the receiving arm farther clear and finish aligning the recovery fingers around the key shaft.
Grasp farther down the exposed shaft, leaving the bow accessible for a better receiving grasp.
Shift the recovery grasp a little farther onto the shaft before closing, to leave the full bow free.
Finish closing on the shaft and test retention with a short vertical lift.
Lift the shaft-held key and rotate its free bow toward the receiving side while maintaining a closed donor grip.
Raise the free bow to transfer height and continue its gradual turn toward the left hand.
Turn the free bow farther toward the receiving side at fixed transfer height, with the left hand still clear.
Finish pointing the free bow toward the left while retaining the shaft; check alignment before advancing the receiver.
Advance the open left hand toward the exposed bow, keeping its height centered and the donor securely closed.
Advance the receiver until the bow sits deeper between its pads, using the centered wrist image and keeping the donor fixed.
Close the receiving fingers on the centered, fully exposed bow; keep the donor closed until retention can be checked.
Hold both wrists fixed and allow the receiving fingers to finish closing around the bow before release.
The receiving fingers closed without visible bow retention. Keep the donor secure and adjust the receiver deeper and toward the key before retrying.
Correct the receiver toward the actual key bow rather than the donor's silver hardware, keeping the fingers open and donor stationary.
Place the bow deeper within the left finger contact region and close cautiously while keeping the donor secure.
Let the receiving fingers settle fully around the exposed bow before testing donor release.
The bow is visibly between the receiving pads. Open the donor gradually while keeping the receiving wrist and grip fixed.
The bow slipped on release. Clear the receiver and recover the key from below, keeping both arms in their own workspace.
Separate the wrists fully and approach the centrally fallen key with the right gripper open, using its new tabletop position.
The key has settled on the left side of center. Clear the right arm and reorient the left hand overhead to recover it within the left workspace.
Use smaller orientation and lift increments after the rejected continuity check; neither arm moved in that rejected chunk.
Continue the left overhead recovery arc toward the fallen key while moving the right hand out of the working area.
Continue a small-increment left overhead approach to the bow in the left workspace; park the right wrist clear.
